108: #!/usr/bin/env bash
109: # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
110: # COMPONENT: CHECK CARD SYNC
111: # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
112: # The authoring card is only useful when four surfaces agree: the card file,
113: # the router that loads it, the leaf inventory that lists it, and the checklist
114: # that sends a reader to a filled example. Each surface can be edited alone,
115: # and a reader then follows a path the others do not describe. This guard
116: # reads all four and fails on the first disagreement.
117: #
118: # Read-only. It writes no file and prints one PASS or FAIL line per check.
119: #
120: # Usage: check-card-sync.sh [--skill-root <path>]
121: # Exit codes: 0 every check passed, 1 one check failed, 2 bad invocation.
122: # ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
123: 
124: set -euo pipefail
125: 
126: SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
127: SKILL_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../../.." && pwd)"
128: 
129: while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
130:     case "$1" in
131:         --skill-root)
132:             [ "$#" -ge 2 ] || { echo "check-card-sync.sh: --skill-root needs a path" >&2; exit 2; }
133:             SKILL_ROOT="$2"
134:             shift 2
135:             ;;
136:         --help|-h)
137:             sed -n '2,14p' "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
138:             exit 0
139:             ;;
140:         *)
141:             echo "check-card-sync.sh: unknown option: $1" >&2
142:             exit 2
143:             ;;
144:     esac
145: done
146: 
147: CARD_REL="references/workflows/spec-authoring-card.md"
148: CARD="$SKILL_ROOT/$CARD_REL"
149: ROUTER="$SKILL_ROOT/SKILL.md"
150: LEAVES="$SKILL_ROOT/leaf-manifest.json"
151: ALIASES="$SKILL_ROOT/leaf-aliases.json"
152: CHECKLIST="$SKILL_ROOT/references/workflows/spec-folder-authoring-checklist.md"
153: MAX_LINES=260
154: STATUS=0
155: 
156: pass() { printf 'PASS %s\n' "$1"; }
157: fail_check() { printf 'FAIL %s: %s\n' "$1" "$2"; STATUS=1; }
158: 
159: # 1. The card exists and stays short enough to read in one pass.
160: if [ ! -f "$CARD" ]; then
161:     fail_check card-exists "missing $CARD_REL"
162: else
163:     LINES=$(wc -l < "$CARD" | tr -d ' ')
164:     if [ "$LINES" -le "$MAX_LINES" ]; then
165:         pass "card-exists ($LINES lines)"
166:     else
167:         fail_check card-length "$LINES lines, limit $MAX_LINES"
168:     fi
169: fi
170: 
171: # 2. Every authoring intent loads the card.
172: for INTENT in PLAN IMPLEMENT INTAKE TEMPLATE_AUTHORING; do
173:     if awk -v intent="$INTENT" '
174:         $0 == "    \"" intent "\": [" { inside = 1; next }
175:         inside && $0 == "    ]," { inside = 0 }
176:         inside && /spec-authoring-card\.md/ { found = 1 }
177:         END { exit(found ? 0 : 1) }
178:     ' "$ROUTER"; then
179:         pass "intent-$INTENT"
180:     else
181:         fail_check "intent-$INTENT" "does not load $CARD_REL"
182:     fi
183: done
184: 
185: # 3. The long guide is reachable only from the on-demand level.
186: GUIDE_IN_MAP=$(awk '
187:     /^RESOURCE_MAP = \{/ { map = 1; next }
188:     map && /^\}$/ { map = 0 }
189:     map && /"references\/templates\/template-guide\.md"/ { n++ }
190:     END { print n + 0 }
191: ' "$ROUTER")
192: GUIDE_ON_DEMAND=$(awk '
193:     /"ON_DEMAND": \[/ { od = 1; next }
194:     od && /^    \],$/ { od = 0 }
195:     od && /"references\/templates\/template-guide\.md"/ { n++ }
196:     END { print n + 0 }
197: ' "$ROUTER")
198: if [ "$GUIDE_IN_MAP" -eq 0 ] && [ "$GUIDE_ON_DEMAND" -eq 1 ]; then
199:     pass guide-on-demand-only
200: else
201:     fail_check guide-on-demand-only "in intent lists: $GUIDE_IN_MAP, in ON_DEMAND: $GUIDE_ON_DEMAND"
202: fi
203: 
204: # 4. The inventory lists the card and the identity projection agrees.
205: if jq -e --arg p "$CARD_REL" '.modes[].leaves | index($p) != null' "$LEAVES" > /dev/null; then
206:     pass leaf-manifest
207: else
208:     fail_check leaf-manifest "does not list $CARD_REL"
209: fi
210: if jq -e --arg p "$CARD_REL" '[.[] | select(.diskPath == $p)] | length > 0' "$ALIASES" > /dev/null; then
211:     pass leaf-aliases
212: else
213:     fail_check leaf-aliases "does not list $CARD_REL"
214: fi
215: 
216: # 5. The checklist sends a reader to a filled example, not the gated source root.
217: if rg -q 'Read templates from `\.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/templates/`' "$CHECKLIST"; then
218:     fail_check checklist "still sends a reader to the templates root"
219: else
220:     pass checklist
221: fi
222: 
223: if [ "$STATUS" -ne 0 ]; then
224:     echo "CARD SYNC FAILED"
225:     exit 1
226: fi
227: echo "CARD SYNC OK"

167: | Risk | The card grows past 260 lines and becomes the guide again | A weak model samples it and the phase changes nothing | The guard fails above 260 lines and the card's own rule forbids a second topic per section |
168: | Risk | A worker copies from a `.tmpl` file and carries tokens into the packet | The packet fails strict or ships a token | The card's step 4 points at rendered examples, and the checklist line is changed in the same phase |

178: - **NFR-P01**: The card stays at or below 260 lines, and each of its sections stays under 20 lines. A section over 20 lines is split or cut.

181: - **NFR-S01**: The card and every brief carry no credential, token or key. Workers inherit provider login from the environment only.
182: 
183: ### Reliability
184: - **NFR-R01**: The guard is deterministic. Two runs on the same tree print the same lines in the same order, and it reads no network and writes no file.

193: 
194: ### Error Scenarios
195: - External service failure: a provider error during a smoke run stops that run. The conductor records the error, retries once after 10 minutes, then records the run as failed.
196: - Network timeout: the smoke run is killed by its captured PID after 30 minutes and recorded as a failed run.

205: | Risk | 6/25 | Auth: N, API: N, Breaking: N, one shared router |
206: | Research | 12/20 | The card must match four scripts and two prior phases |
207: | Multi-Agent | 8/15 | Workstreams: card, router, guard, three smoke runs, one review |
208: | Coordination | 8/15 | Dependencies: phases 003 and 004 closed, launch preconditions |
209: | **Total** | **45/100** | **Level 3** |

214: 
215: | Risk ID | Description | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |
216: |---------|-------------|--------|------------|------------|
217: | R-001 | The card repeats the guide's scope and length | M | M | The 260-line guard, plus one topic per section |
218: | R-002 | A router edit lands in the wrong intent block | H | L | Each edit carries its intent header in the old text, so a wrong block cannot match |
219: | R-003 | The inventory fix writes outside system-spec-kit | H | L | `--skill system-spec-kit` scopes the run, and T006 reads the changed-file list |
220: | R-004 | A smoke run passes strict with tokens still in the packet | M | H | Metric M2 counts tokens separately from M1, and a run needs both to count as a pass |
221: 
222: ---
223: 
224: ## 11. USER STORIES
225: 
226: ### US-001: One short card is the default (Priority: P0)
227: 
228: **As a** weak authoring model, **I want** one short card that names the files, the steps and the checks, **so that** I finish a packet without sampling a long guide.
229: 
230: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ### US-002: Drift fails, not warns (Priority: P1)
235: 
236: **As the** operator, **I want** the card, the router, the inventory and the checklist checked by one command, **so that** a later edit cannot quietly undo this phase.
237: 
238: **Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).
239: 
240: ---

243: ## 12. OPEN QUESTIONS

245: - None that block this phase. Every choice it needs is frozen in `goal.md` section 1.
246: - The card's exact text is frozen in `plan.md` section 3. A change to that text is an amendment to this phase, not an executor choice.
247: <!-- /ANCHOR:questions -->

255: - **Verification Checklist**: See `tasks.md`
256: - **Decision Records**: See `plan.md` section L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD

708: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
709: 
710: ### ADR-001: One card replaces the guide as the default load
711: 
712: **Status**: Accepted
713: 
714: **Context**: Four authoring intents load a 1,200-line guide. A weak model samples a long doc and copies the nearest example. The guide also mixes template-authoring rules with packet-authoring rules, so a model that only needs to fill a scaffold reads rules about files it must not touch.
715: 
716: **Decision**: The four intents load a 170-line card. The guide stays in the `ON_DEMAND` list, so a reader who asks for the full guide still gets it.
717: 
718: **Consequences**:
719: - A weak model gets one screen of rules and a command per step.
720: - A reader who needs the guide's depth must ask for it. The card names the guide once, so the path is visible.
721: 
722: **Alternatives Rejected**:
723: - Shortening the guide in place: it would still be the default load, and phase 2 owns its defect repairs.
724: - Two cards, one for templates and one for packets: it doubles the surface the guard must read for a difference only a template author sees.
725: 
726: ### ADR-002: Generate the inventory, never hand-edit it
727: 
728: **Status**: Accepted
729: 
730: **Context**: `leaf-manifest.json` is byte-checked by `generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --check`, and `leaf-aliases.json` is checked as its projection by `ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs`. A hand edit passes one and fails the other.
731: 
732: **Decision**: Run `generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --write` then `ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs --fix --skill system-spec-kit`. The `--skill` scope keeps the write inside this skill.
733: 
734: **Consequences**:
735: - Both files agree with the tree and with each other.
736: - The fix command also reports other root metadata violations. A non-zero exit with the two files written is recorded, not treated as a write failure.
737: 
738: **Alternatives Rejected**:
739: - Adding the card row by hand: it survives until the next generator run and then disappears.
740: 
741: ### ADR-003: A shell guard plus one vitest test, not a validator rule
742: 
743: **Status**: Accepted
744: 
745: **Context**: The surfaces are skill files, not a spec folder. `validate.sh` reads a packet, so it cannot check a router. The post-edit router runs per edited file and returns no finding on failure, so it cannot hold a repo-wide invariant.
746: 
747: **Decision**: `runtime/cli/spec/check-card-sync.sh` holds the invariant and `runtime/cli/tests/card-sync.vitest.ts` runs it in the suite. The script is also listed in `runtime/cli/spec/README.md`.
748: 
749: **Consequences**:
750: - One command answers whether the four surfaces agree.
751: - The check costs one process per suite run and reads five files.
752: 
753: **Alternatives Rejected**:
754: - A validator rule: it would need a packet argument it does not have.
755: - A post-edit hook: a hook that cannot block is not a guard.

133: ## 4. READ BEFORE YOU WRITE

136:

144: ## 5. ONE ACTION PER SECTION
145: 
146: Each section does one job. Write one idea per paragraph. Do not repeat the same fact in two sections.
147: 
148: - `spec.md` states the problem, the scope, the requirements and the success criteria.
149: - `plan.md` states the approach, the files to change, the test plan and the dependencies.
150: - `tasks.md` states the ordered actions.
151: - `implementation-summary.md` states what changed and how it was checked. Write it last.

158: ## 6. THE PLAN SHAPE
159: 
160: A plan has 3 or 4 steps. More than 4 steps means the feature is too large for one packet. Split it or raise the level.
161: 
162: Each step carries three lines:
163: 1. What the step does.
164: 2. The acceptance line: what is true when the step is done.
165: 3. The verify command: the command a reader runs, and the text it prints.

169: 
170: Acceptance: `--quiet` is accepted and the default output is unchanged.
171: Verify: `bash script.sh --quiet` prints one line.
172: ```

195: ## 8. FILL EVERY TOKEN
196: 
197: A scaffold stamped `v2.3` or later carries tokens. A token starts with `[YOUR_VALUE_HERE:` and ends at the next closing bracket. Replace the whole token, brackets included, with real content. Do not leave a token in a finished packet.
198: 
199: If you cannot answer a question the token asks, write an open question instead. It starts with `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION:` and ends at the next closing bracket.
200: 
201: A token in a packet whose `spec.md` says `Status: Draft` is a warning, so strict validation can pass with tokens still in the file. A token in any other status is an error. Do not use the warning as permission. Count the tokens.
202: 
203: Acceptance: the count is 0.
204: Verify: `rg -o '\[YOUR_VALUE_HERE: ' <packet folder>/spec.md <packet folder>/plan.md <packet folder>/tasks.md | wc -l` prints 0.

215: 
216: When it fails, read the first failing rule. Fix that rule only. Run the command again. Stop after three fixes on the same rule and write the rule and the error in the packet's `goal.md`.
217: 
218: Acceptance: the command prints `RESULT: PASSED` and `Errors: 0`.
219: Verify: `bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh <packet folder> --strict | tail -1` prints `RESULT: PASSED`.

221: ## 10. CLOSE
222: 
223: A packet is closeable when:
224: - every required file exists for its level
225: - every token is filled or replaced by an open question
226: - `tasks.md` has no `[ ]` and no `[B]` line
227: - `implementation-summary.md` names the files that changed
228: - `validate.sh --strict` prints `RESULT: PASSED`
229: 
230: Acceptance: all five are true.
231: Verify: run the five commands in this card in order, then run the validator once more.

233: ## 11. WHEN TO STOP AND ASK
234: 
235: Stop and write the question in `goal.md` when:
236: - two documents in the packet state opposite rules
237: - a command in the plan would write outside the packet folder
238: - the validator fails on the same rule after three fixes
239: - the feature needs more than 4 plan steps
240: 
241: Do not guess. A written question is a finished step. A guess is a defect.

538: 3. Delete `spec-authoring-card.md`, `check-card-sync.sh` and `card-sync.vitest.ts` after their paths are in `goal.md` section 4.
539: 4. Run `generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --write $S` and `ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs --fix --skill system-spec-kit` to rebuild the inventory from the restored tree.
540: 5. Run `git status --porcelain` and compare with `scratch/status-start.txt`.
541: 6. Record the rollback in `goal.md` section 4.
542: 
543: ### Data Reversal
544: - **Has data migrations?** No
545: - **Reversal procedure**: N/A, the two inventory files are generated and rebuild from the tree

547: 
548: ---
549: 
550: 
551: ---

553: <!-- ANCHOR:dependency-graph -->
554: ## L3: DEPENDENCY GRAPH
555: 
556: ```
557: ┌──────────┐     ┌──────────┐     ┌───────────┐     ┌──────────┐
558: │  Setup   │────►│   Card   │────►│  Router   │────►│ Inventory│
559: └──────────┘     └──────────┘     └─────┬─────┘     └────┬─────┘
560:                                         │                │
561:                               ┌─────────▼────────┐       │
562:                               │ Checklist, Tmpl  │       │
563:                               └─────────┬────────┘       │
564:                                         │                │
565:                               ┌─────────▼────────────────▼─┐
566:                               │      Guard and wiring      │
567:                               └─────────────┬──────────────┘
568:                                             │
569:                               ┌─────────────▼──────────────┐
570:                               │ Vocabulary, smoke runs,    │
571:                               │ review, close              │
572:                               └────────────────────────────┘
573: ```
574: 
575: ### Dependency Matrix
576: 
577: | Component | Depends On | Produces | Blocks |
578: |-----------|------------|----------|--------|
579: | Setup | Launch preconditions | Start commit, checks | Card |
580: | Card | Setup | `spec-authoring-card.md` | Router |
581: | Router | Card | Four intent rows | Inventory, guard |
582: | Inventory | Router | Two generated files | Guard |
583: | Guard | Router, Inventory, Checklist, Template | `check-card-sync.sh` | Wiring, vocabulary |
584: | Vocabulary | Guard | A clean card | Smoke runs |
585: | Smoke runs | Vocabulary | `scratch/card-bench/` | Review |
586: | Review | Smoke runs | Findings | Phase close |
587: <!-- /ANCHOR:dependency-graph -->
588: 
589: ---
590: 
591: <!-- ANCHOR:critical-path -->
592: ## L3: CRITICAL PATH
593: 
594: 1. **Card and router** - 1 hour - CRITICAL
595: 2. **Smoke runs** - 1 to 2 hours - CRITICAL
596: 3. **Review and close** - 30 minutes - CRITICAL
597: 
598: **Total Critical Path**: about 2.5 to 3.5 hours
599: 
600: **Parallel Opportunities**:
601: - The checklist edit and the template edit run together, because they touch different files and neither reads the other.
602: - The inventory regeneration runs after both. The generator reads every file under `references/`, and the checklist edit writes one of them, so a generator run that starts before the edit finishes would read the old file.
603: <!-- /ANCHOR:critical-path -->
604: 
605: ---
606: 
607: <!-- ANCHOR:milestones -->
608: ## L3: MILESTONES
609: 
610: | Milestone | Description | Success Criteria | Target |
611: |-----------|-------------|------------------|--------|
612: | M1 | Setup done | T001 to T003 marked `[x]` with evidence | Start of phase |
613: | M2 | Card and router done | The card exists at 170 lines and four intents load it | Mid phase |
614: | M3 | Guard green | `CARD SYNC OK` and the vitest test passes | Mid phase |
615: | M4 | Phase closeable | Every acceptance criterion `Met` | End of phase |
616: <!-- /ANCHOR:milestones -->
617: 
618: ---
619: 
620: <!-- ANCHOR:ai-execution -->
621: ## AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL
622: 
623: Written for the executing swarm. Follow each rule as written. Where a rule and your own judgment disagree, follow the rule and record the disagreement in `goal.md` section 4.
624: 
625: ### Roles
626: - **Conductor**: one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session that is not itself running inside OpenCode, because `cli-opencode` refuses a dispatch from inside OpenCode. It dispatches workers, runs every verify command, edits the nine declared paths, and keeps `goal.md` section 4 current.
627: - **Worker**: one `opencode2 run` dispatch on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`. One worker authors one Level 1 packet, then stops.
628: - **Reviewer**: one read-only frontier review through `cli-codex` at phase close. It writes nothing.
629: 
630: ### Pre-Task Checklist
631: - [ ] Read this phase's `spec.md`, this plan and `tasks.md` before the first edit
632: - [ ] Read `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md` sections 3 and 4 before composing the first worker command
633: - [ ] Confirm the working directory is the build worktree recorded in `../goal.md` section 4, never the main checkout
634: - [ ] Confirm `opencode2 models --standalone` lists `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`
635: - [ ] Save every brief to `scratch/briefs/<task-id>.txt` before dispatching it
636: 
637: ### Execution Rules
638: 
639: | Rule | Requirement |
640: |------|-------------|
641: | TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. No two tasks write the same file, so no task is marked `[P]` |
642: | TASK-SCOPE | A worker writes only the paths under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS in its brief |
643: | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
644: | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number. Each edit below names its old text |
645: | TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |
646: | TASK-COPY | The card is copied from section 3.1, never retyped. A retyped card fails the vocabulary check or the line count |
647: 
648: ### Worker Brief Skeleton
649: 
650: Every brief starts with this block, word for word, with the two paths filled in:
651: 
652: ```text
653: GATE 3 IS PRE-RESOLVED. DO NOT ASK THE DOCUMENTATION-SCOPE QUESTION.
654: 
655: You are a non-interactive dispatched worker. AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 and
656: SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 are set in your environment, which this repository's AGENTS.md
657: defines as the autonomous child-dispatch exemption: the spec-folder question is pre-resolved
658: and MUST NOT be asked. No answer can reach you, because nobody is at a prompt.
659: 
660: Your write authority is already bound. The spec folder is:
661:   <the packet folder this task names>
662: 
663: Proceed directly to the work. Do not print A/B/C/D options. Do not stop to confirm anything.
664: A failed edit match means a stale anchor: re-read the file and retry; halt only after three
665: failures on the same file.
666: Your task is complete only when files exist on disk and the verification command has been run.
667: 
668: ROLE: <one line, the focused persona for this task>
669: 
670: ALLOWED WRITE PATHS:
671:   <the one folder this task names>
672: 
673: BANNED OPERATIONS: git commit, git push, git checkout, git switch, git branch, git reset,
674: git stash, rm, mv, create.sh outside the task's stated command, generate-context.js,
675: /speckit:save, and any edit to a file not listed under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS.
676: ```
677: 
678: The role line is a focused persona summary in place of a full agent file, the small-context exception that `cli-opencode` rule 18 allows. It is declared here as that exception.
679: 
680: ### Dispatch Command
681: 
682: ```bash
683: cd "$WORKTREE" && SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 opencode2 run --standalone \
684:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json \
685:   "$(cat "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/$TASK.txt")" </dev/null > "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$TASK.jsonl" 2>&1 &
686: PID=$!; wait "$PID"; kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$PID" 2>/dev/null
687: ```
688: 
689: `PHASE` is this folder's path and `WORKTREE` is the build worktree. Never kill by a name pattern. Kill only the captured PID.
690: 
691: ### Status Reporting Format
692: 
693: ```text
694: [T###] DONE | BLOCKED - one line of evidence
695: ```
696: 
697: Written as a row in the progress table of `goal.md` section 4.
698: 
699: ### Blocked Task Protocol
700: 1. Restore any file the task changed with `git restore --source=<start commit> -- <file>`.
701: 2. Mark the task `[B]` in `tasks.md` with the failing command and the first line of its output.
702: 3. Re-dispatch at most twice with the brief corrected for what failed. After the third failure on the same task, leave it `[B]` and continue with the next task.
703: 4. Stop the phase when two tasks are blocked, and write `STOP` with both task IDs in `goal.md` section 4.
704: <!-- /ANCHOR:ai-execution -->
705: 
706: ---
707: 
708: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
709: 
710: ### ADR-001: One card replaces the guide as the default load
711: 
712: **Status**: Accepted
713: 
714: **Context**: Four authoring intents load a 1,200-line guide. A weak model samples a long doc and copies the nearest example. The guide also mixes template-authoring rules with packet-authoring rules, so a model that only needs to fill a scaffold reads rules about files it must not touch.
715: 
716: **Decision**: The four intents load a 170-line card. The guide stays in the `ON_DEMAND` list, so a reader who asks for the full guide still gets it.
717: 
718: **Consequences**:
719: - A weak model gets one screen of rules and a command per step.
720: - A reader who needs the guide's depth must ask for it. The card names the guide once, so the path is visible.
721: 
722: **Alternatives Rejected**:
723: - Shortening the guide in place: it would still be the default load, and phase 2 owns its defect repairs.
724: - Two cards, one for templates and one for packets: it doubles the surface the guard must read for a difference only a template author sees.
725: 
726: ### ADR-002: Generate the inventory, never hand-edit it
727: 
728: **Status**: Accepted
729: 
730: **Context**: `leaf-manifest.json` is byte-checked by `generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --check`, and `leaf-aliases.json` is checked as its projection by `ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs`. A hand edit passes one and fails the other.
731: 
732: **Decision**: Run `generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --write` then `ci-skill-root-metadata.cjs --fix --skill system-spec-kit`. The `--skill` scope keeps the write inside this skill.
733: 
734: **Consequences**:
735: - Both files agree with the tree and with each other.
736: - The fix command also reports other root metadata violations. A non-zero exit with the two files written is recorded, not treated as a write failure.
737: 
738: **Alternatives Rejected**:
739: - Adding the card row by hand: it survives until the next generator run and then disappears.
740: 
741: ### ADR-003: A shell guard plus one vitest test, not a validator rule
742: 
743: **Status**: Accepted
744: 
745: **Context**: The surfaces are skill files, not a spec folder. `validate.sh` reads a packet, so it cannot check a router. The post-edit router runs per edited file and returns no finding on failure, so it cannot hold a repo-wide invariant.
746: 
747: **Decision**: `runtime/cli/spec/check-card-sync.sh` holds the invariant and `runtime/cli/tests/card-sync.vitest.ts` runs it in the suite. The script is also listed in `runtime/cli/spec/README.md`.
748: 
749: **Consequences**:
750: - One command answers whether the four surfaces agree.
751: - The check costs one process per suite run and reads five files.
752: 
753: **Alternatives Rejected**:
754: - A validator rule: it would need a packet argument it does not have.
755: - A post-edit hook: a hook that cannot block is not a guard.
756: 
757: ---

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# COMPONENT: CHECK PLACEHOLDERS
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Scan spec folder .md files for remaining bracket placeholder
# Patterns after upgrade-level.sh + auto-populate.
# Bash 3.2+ compatible (macOS and Linux).
#
# This is the broad post-edit scan the quality hook runs: any bracket that
# still looks like a template placeholder. The validator rule at
# rules/check-placeholders.sh is narrower on purpose, flagging only the two
# canonical markers, so the two are not the same check with two homes.

set -euo pipefail

VERSION="1.0.0"

# Colors (disabled for non-TTY)
if [[ -t 1 ]]; then
    RED='\033[0;31m' GREEN='\033[0;32m' YELLOW='\033[1;33m' BOLD='\033[1m' NC='\033[0m'
else
    RED='' GREEN='' YELLOW='' BOLD='' NC=''
fi

# ─── Usage ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
    cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") <spec-folder> [OPTIONS]

Scan a spec folder for remaining bracket placeholder patterns.

Arguments:
  <spec-folder>    Path to spec folder (e.g., specs/042-feature/)

Options:
  --json           Output results in JSON format
  --verbose        Show each match with file and line number
  --help, -h       Show this help message

Exit codes:
  0  No placeholders found (PASS)
  1  Placeholders found (FAIL)
  2  Invalid arguments or folder not found

Examples:
  $(basename "$0") specs/042-feature/
  $(basename "$0") specs/042-feature/ --verbose
  $(basename "$0") specs/042-feature/ --json
EOF
}

# ─── Args ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FOLDER_PATH=""
JSON_MODE=false
VERBOSE=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --json)     JSON_MODE=true; shift ;;
        --verbose)  VERBOSE=true; shift ;;
        --help|-h)  usage; exit 0 ;;
        -*)         echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
        *)
            if [[ -z "$FOLDER_PATH" ]]; then
                FOLDER_PATH="$1"
            else
                echo "Error: unexpected argument '$1'" >&2
                usage >&2
                exit 2
            fi
            shift
            ;;
    esac
done

if [[ -z "$FOLDER_PATH" ]]; then
    echo "Error: spec folder path required" >&2
    usage >&2
    exit 2
fi

# Normalize trailing slash
FOLDER_PATH="${FOLDER_PATH%/}"

if [[ ! -d "$FOLDER_PATH" ]]; then
    echo "Error: folder not found: $FOLDER_PATH" >&2
    exit 2
fi

# ─── Placeholder patterns ────────────────────────────────────
# Match bracket patterns that look like template placeholders:
#   [Response time target], [Low/Med/High], [Component A],
#   [YOUR_VALUE_HERE], [PLACEHOLDER], etc.
#
# The templates write their stubs with the example inline, as in
# [Response time target - e.g., <200ms p95], [Uptime target - e.g., 99.9%]
# and [What problem we're solving], so the body admits < > + % and the
# apostrophe too. Without them those stubs pass the scan unfilled.
PLACEHOLDER_BODY="[A-Za-z0-9 /,._<>+%'-]"
#
# Exclude patterns that are NOT placeholders:
#   [x] / [ ] (checkbox), [P0] / [P1] / [P2] (priority tags),
#   [SPECKIT...] (markers), [ANCHOR...] (anchors),
#   [EVIDENCE...] (checklist evidence), [W:...] (workstream),
#   [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] (spec markers), [B] (blocked task)
#
# Also exclude lines where brackets appear inside code blocks
# (backtick-wrapped) since those describe placeholder concepts
# Rather than being actual unfilled placeholders.

TOTAL=0
MATCHES=""

# Process each .md file (skip backup/temp directories)
while IFS= read -r file; do
    # Skip backup directories and non-template subfolders.
    # Memory/ contains generated session context markdown that legitimately
    # Uses bracketed TOC links (e.g., [CONTINUE SESSION]); scratch/ is temp.
    case "$file" in
        */.backup-*) continue ;;
        */memory/*) continue ;;
        */scratch/*) continue ;;
        # research/ and review/ hold the deep loops' own output: iteration files,
        # dashboards and syntheses their workflow writes and regenerates, where
        # bracketed status text such as [None yet] is the reducer's format rather
        # than an unfilled template. The validator's placeholder rule reads only
        # the authored docs, so this scan matches it.
        */research/*) continue ;;
        */review/*) continue ;;
    esac

    line_num=0
    while IFS= read -r line; do
        line_num=$((line_num + 1))

        # Skip lines inside code fences or with backtick-wrapped brackets
        case "$line" in
            '```'*) continue ;;
            *'`['*) continue ;;
        esac

        # Skip HTML comments
        case "$line" in
            *'<!--'*'-->'*) continue ;;
        esac

        # Match bracket patterns that look like placeholders
        # Use grep to find [Something here] patterns
        if echo "$line" | grep -qE "\[[A-Z]${PLACEHOLDER_BODY}+\]" 2>/dev/null; then
            # Exclude known non-placeholder patterns
            cleaned="$line"
            # Remove known safe patterns before re-checking
            cleaned=$(echo "$cleaned" | sed -E \
                -e 's/\[x\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[ \]//g' \
                -e 's/\[P[0-2]\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[B\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[SPECKIT[^]]*\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[ANCHOR[^]]*\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[EVIDENCE[^]]*\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[NEEDS CLARIFICATION\]//g' \
                -e 's/\[W:[^]]*\]//g' \
                -e 's/`[^`]*`//g' \
                -e 's/\[[^]]*\]\(//g' \
            )

            # Check if any placeholder-like patterns remain after cleanup
            if echo "$cleaned" | grep -qE "\[[A-Z]${PLACEHOLDER_BODY}{2,}\]" 2>/dev/null; then
                TOTAL=$((TOTAL + 1))
                match_text=$(echo "$line" | grep -oE "\[[A-Z]${PLACEHOLDER_BODY}{2,}\]" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
                if [[ "$VERBOSE" == "true" ]]; then
                    MATCHES="${MATCHES}  ${file}:${line_num}: ${match_text}\n"
                fi
            fi
        fi
    done < "$file"
done < <(find "$FOLDER_PATH" -name "*.md" -type f 2>/dev/null | sort)

# ─── Output ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
if [[ "$JSON_MODE" == "true" ]]; then
    if [[ $TOTAL -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo "{\"status\":\"PASS\",\"placeholders\":0,\"folder\":\"$FOLDER_PATH\"}"
    else
        echo "{\"status\":\"FAIL\",\"placeholders\":$TOTAL,\"folder\":\"$FOLDER_PATH\"}"
    fi
else
    if [[ $TOTAL -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo -e "${GREEN}${BOLD}PASS${NC} — Zero placeholder patterns found in ${FOLDER_PATH}"
    else
        echo -e "${RED}${BOLD}FAIL${NC} — ${TOTAL} placeholder pattern(s) found in ${FOLDER_PATH}" >&2
        if [[ "$VERBOSE" == "true" && -n "$MATCHES" ]]; then
            echo ""
            echo -e "$MATCHES"
        fi
    fi
fi

# Exit code: 0 = pass, 1 = fail
if [[ $TOTAL -eq 0 ]]; then
    exit 0
else
    exit 1
fi

state.output:
Think of it as a "project folder" for AI-assisted development - it keeps context organized and enables session continuity.

### Activation Triggers

**MANDATORY for ALL file modifications:**
- Code files: JS, TS, Python, CSS, HTML
- Documentation: Markdown, README, guides
- Configuration: JSON, YAML, TOML, env templates
- Templates, knowledge base, build/tooling files

**Request patterns that trigger activation:**
- "Add/implement/create [feature]"
- "Fix/update/refactor [code]"
- "Modify/change [configuration]"
- Positive keywords include add, implement, fix, update, create, modify, rename, delete and configure. The authoritative Gate 3 classifier intentionally omits `analyze`, `decompose` and `phase` from positive triggers; `analyze` is a read-only disqualifier unless a real write, memory-save or resume trigger is also present.

**Example triggers:**
- "Add email validation to the signup form" → Level 1-2
- "Refactor the authentication module" → Level 2-3
- "Fix the button alignment bug" → Level 1
- "Implement user dashboard with analytics" → Level 3

### When NOT to Use

- Pure exploration/reading (no file modifications)
- Single typo fixes (<5 characters in one file)
- Whitespace-only changes
- Auto-generated file updates (package-lock.json)
- User explicitly selects Option D (skip documentation)

**Rule of thumb:** If modifying ANY file content → Activate this skill.
Status: ✅ This requirement applies immediately once file edits are requested.

### Distributed Governance Rule

Any agent writing authored spec folder docs (`spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `acceptance-criteria.md`, `implementation-summary.md`, `decision-record.md`, `handover.md`, `review-report.md`, `debug-delegation.md`, `resource-map.md`, `goal.md`, `before-after.md`, `timeline.md`, `roadmap.md` (the last six optional)) MUST use contract-backed templates through `create.sh` or the inline renderer. `goal.md` may also come from `/create:goal`, whose per-kind templates are parity-checked copies of `goal.md.tmpl`. This is a workflow-required gate, not a runtime hook: run `bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh <spec-folder> --strict` after authored spec-doc writes and before completion claims, then route continuity updates through /speckit:save. Deep-research workflow-owned packet markdown (`research/iterations/*.md`, `research/deep-research-*.md`, and progressive `research/research.md` loop updates) is exempt from that generic per-write rule; `/deep:research` must instead run targeted strict validation after every `spec.md` mutation it performs. @deep-research retains exclusive write access for `research/research.md`; @debug retains exclusive write access for `debug-delegation.md`.

- `handover.md` stays in the canonical recovery ladder and is maintained through `/speckit:save` handover_state routing using the handover template for initial creation.
- `review-report.md` remains owned by `@deep-review` when deep review workflows synthesize findings.
- `resource-map.md` is a lazy add-on in every level contract; render it with the inline gate renderer when a packet wants a lean file ledger alongside `implementation-summary.md`. The deep loops write their own evidence ledger of the same name into their artifact directory, not the packet root.

### Utility Template Triggers

| Template              | Trigger Keywords                                                                                                              | Action                    |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `handover.md`         | "handover", "next session", "continue later", "pass context", "ending session", "save state", "multi-session", "for next AI"  | Suggest `/speckit:save` handover maintenance |
| `debug-delegation.md` | "stuck", "can't fix", "tried everything", "same error", "fresh eyes", "hours on this", "still failing", "need help debugging" | Suggest Task-tool debug delegation |

**Rule:** When detected, proactively suggest the appropriate action.

---

## 2. SMART ROUTING

### Resource Domains

This skill uses simple intent/domain routing, not keyed runtime resource routing. It does not select whole `references/<key>/` or `assets/<key>/` subtrees from project, mode, stack, or model signals. Instead, the router discovers markdown resources recursively from `references/` and `assets/`, then applies intent scoring from `RESOURCE_MAP` to load real, guarded resources from the current inventory. Keep this section domain-focused rather than static file inventories.

- `references/retrieval/` for the trigger-index lookup and the ripgrep recipes.
- `references/memory/` for continuity save workflows, trigger-phrase behavior, and the shared embedding stack.
- `references/templates/` for level selection, template selection, and structure guides.
- `references/validation/` for checklist policy, verification rules, decision formats, and template compliance contracts.
- `references/structure/` for folder organization and sub-folder versioning.
- `references/workflows/` for command workflows, shared intake, rename procedures, and worked examples.
- `references/debugging/` for troubleshooting and root-cause methodology.
- `references/cli/` for daemon CLI behavior, shared smart-router behavior, and continuity handback contracts.
- `references/config/` for runtime environment configuration and launcher/lease contracts.
- `assets/*.md` for shared decision matrices, template mapping, and parallel dispatch support.

**Typed leaf projection (fleet routing standard).** system-spec-kit is a normal, registry-less single-mode skill whose sole workflow mode is `system-spec-kit` (there is no `mode-registry.json`). Its router routes ONLY into the `references/` and `assets/` doc corpora, so those are the only routable leaves: every one is enumerated in `leaf-manifest.json`, generated from `leaf-manifest.config.json` (`generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --write .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit`; byte-stable under `--check`). `leaf-aliases.json` binds each router-emitted root-relative path (e.g. `references/memory/memory-system.md`) to its typed `(system-spec-kit, leafResourceId)` identity so a deterministic router replay recovers real typed pairs against the manifest. The `RESOURCE_MAP` below names every leaf in that manifest under at least one intent, so each reference and asset is reachable through the router as well as by browsing; the manifest stays the inventory, and a leaf added to the corpus without an intent is a routing gap to close, not a browse-only tier. The rest of the package is deliberately NOT routable: `runtime/cli/`, `runtime/`, `shared/`, `templates/`, `changelog/` and other engine dirs are the spec-kit runtime, and `feature-catalog/` + `manual-testing-playbook/` are runtime-engine capability docs and behavior-test fixtures — no `RESOURCE_MAP` intent selects them, so they are excluded from `leafRoots` and never appear in the manifest. This is an intentionally thin router: it maps spec-folder workflow intents (plan, implement, complete, memory, phase, hooks, …) to a small set of reference docs, while the large playbook chiefly exercises validation and generator behavior rather than doc routing (most scenarios carry empty typed gold). Regenerate `leaf-manifest.json` and keep `leaf-aliases.json` in sync whenever the `references/` or `assets/` corpus changes.

### Template and Script Sources of Truth

- Level definitions and template size guidance: level specifications reference
- Template usage and composition rules: [template-guide.md](./references/templates/template-guide.md)

content.text:
Think of it as a "project folder" for AI-assisted development - it keeps context organized and enables session continuity.

### Activation Triggers

**MANDATORY for ALL file modifications:**
- Code files: JS, TS, Python, CSS, HTML
- Documentation: Markdown, README, guides
- Configuration: JSON, YAML, TOML, env templates
- Templates, knowledge base, build/tooling files

**Request patterns that trigger activation:**
- "Add/implement/create [feature]"
- "Fix/update/refactor [code]"
- "Modify/change [configuration]"
- Positive keywords include add, implement, fix, update, create, modify, rename, delete and configure. The authoritative Gate 3 classifier intentionally omits `analyze`, `decompose` and `phase` from positive triggers; `analyze` is a read-only disqualifier unless a real write, memory-save or resume trigger is also present.

**Example triggers:**
- "Add email validation to the signup form" → Level 1-2
- "Refactor the authentication module" → Level 2-3
- "Fix the button alignment bug" → Level 1
- "Implement user dashboard with analytics" → Level 3

### When NOT to Use

- Pure exploration/reading (no file modifications)
- Single typo fixes (<5 characters in one file)
- Whitespace-only changes
- Auto-generated file updates (package-lock.json)
- User explicitly selects Option D (skip documentation)

**Rule of thumb:** If modifying ANY file content → Activate this skill.
Status: ✅ This requirement applies immediately once file edits are requested.

### Distributed Governance Rule

Any agent writing authored spec folder docs (`spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, `acceptance-criteria.md`, `implementation-summary.md`, `decision-record.md`, `handover.md`, `review-report.md`, `debug-delegation.md`, `resource-map.md`, `goal.md`, `before-after.md`, `timeline.md`, `roadmap.md` (the last six optional)) MUST use contract-backed templates through `create.sh` or the inline renderer. `goal.md` may also come from `/create:goal`, whose per-kind templates are parity-checked copies of `goal.md.tmpl`. This is a workflow-required gate, not a runtime hook: run `bash .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/validate.sh <spec-folder> --strict` after authored spec-doc writes and before completion claims, then route continuity updates through /speckit:save. Deep-research workflow-owned packet markdown (`research/iterations/*.md`, `research/deep-research-*.md`, and progressive `research/research.md` loop updates) is exempt from that generic per-write rule; `/deep:research` must instead run targeted strict validation after every `spec.md` mutation it performs. @deep-research retains exclusive write access for `research/research.md`; @debug retains exclusive write access for `debug-delegation.md`.

- `handover.md` stays in the canonical recovery ladder and is maintained through `/speckit:save` handover_state routing using the handover template for initial creation.
- `review-report.md` remains owned by `@deep-review` when deep review workflows synthesize findings.
- `resource-map.md` is a lazy add-on in every level contract; render it with the inline gate renderer when a packet wants a lean file ledger alongside `implementation-summary.md`. The deep loops write their own evidence ledger of the same name into their artifact directory, not the packet root.

### Utility Template Triggers

| Template              | Trigger Keywords                                                                                                              | Action                    |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `handover.md`         | "handover", "next session", "continue later", "pass context", "ending session", "save state", "multi-session", "for next AI"  | Suggest `/speckit:save` handover maintenance |
| `debug-delegation.md` | "stuck", "can't fix", "tried everything", "same error", "fresh eyes", "hours on this", "still failing", "need help debugging" | Suggest Task-tool debug delegation |

**Rule:** When detected, proactively suggest the appropriate action.

---

## 2. SMART ROUTING

### Resource Domains

This skill uses simple intent/domain routing, not keyed runtime resource routing. It does not select whole `references/<key>/` or `assets/<key>/` subtrees from project, mode, stack, or model signals. Instead, the router discovers markdown resources recursively from `references/` and `assets/`, then applies intent scoring from `RESOURCE_MAP` to load real, guarded resources from the current inventory. Keep this section domain-focused rather than static file inventories.

- `references/retrieval/` for the trigger-index lookup and the ripgrep recipes.
- `references/memory/` for continuity save workflows, trigger-phrase behavior, and the shared embedding stack.
- `references/templates/` for level selection, template selection, and structure guides.
- `references/validation/` for checklist policy, verification rules, decision formats, and template compliance contracts.
- `references/structure/` for folder organization and sub-folder versioning.
- `references/workflows/` for command workflows, shared intake, rename procedures, and worked examples.
- `references/debugging/` for troubleshooting and root-cause methodology.
- `references/cli/` for daemon CLI behavior, shared smart-router behavior, and continuity handback contracts.
- `references/config/` for runtime environment configuration and launcher/lease contracts.
- `assets/*.md` for shared decision matrices, template mapping, and parallel dispatch support.

**Typed leaf projection (fleet routing standard).** system-spec-kit is a normal, registry-less single-mode skill whose sole workflow mode is `system-spec-kit` (there is no `mode-registry.json`). Its router routes ONLY into the `references/` and `assets/` doc corpora, so those are the only routable leaves: every one is enumerated in `leaf-manifest.json`, generated from `leaf-manifest.config.json` (`generate-leaf-manifest.cjs --write .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit`; byte-stable under `--check`). `leaf-aliases.json` binds each router-emitted root-relative path (e.g. `references/memory/memory-system.md`) to its typed `(system-spec-kit, leafResourceId)` identity so a deterministic router replay recovers real typed pairs against the manifest. The `RESOURCE_MAP` below names every leaf in that manifest under at least one intent, so each reference and asset is reachable through the router as well as by browsing; the manifest stays the inventory, and a leaf added to the corpus without an intent is a routing gap to close, not a browse-only tier. The rest of the package is deliberately NOT routable: `runtime/cli/`, `runtime/`, `shared/`, `templates/`, `changelog/` and other engine dirs are the spec-kit runtime, and `feature-catalog/` + `manual-testing-playbook/` are runtime-engine capability docs and behavior-test fixtures — no `RESOURCE_MAP` intent selects them, so they are excluded from `leafRoots` and never appear in the manifest. This is an intentionally thin router: it maps spec-folder workflow intents (plan, implement, complete, memory, phase, hooks, …) to a small set of reference docs, while the large playbook chiefly exercises validation and generator behavior rather than doc routing (most scenarios carry empty typed gold). Regenerate `leaf-manifest.json` and keep `leaf-aliases.json` in sync whenever the `references/` or `assets/` corpus changes.

- Template usage and composition rules: [template-guide.md](./references/templates/template-guide.md)

- Memory save JSON schema and workflow contracts: [save-workflow.md](./references/memory/save-workflow.md)
- Nested packet changelog workflow: [nested-changelog.md](./references/workflows/nested-changelog.md)

247:- **`codex exec` defaults to `--sandbox read-only`** — file-modification tasks silently no-op (the agent plans changes but cannot write them). Pass `--sandbox workspace-write`; for headless no-prompt execution use top-level `-a never` before `exec` or `-c approval_policy=never`.
248:- **`--search` is a top-level flag, not an `exec` flag** — enable live web search as `codex --search exec …` (it precedes the subcommand). On codex ≥ 0.144 `codex exec --search` hard-fails with `unexpected argument '--search'` (older 0.125 builds accepted it), so treat any `exec … --search` example as stale. Without it, `codex exec` has no web access and answers from training data only — every dispatch needing live data (latest versions, repo facts, advisories) MUST use `codex --search exec …`.
251:- **`--sandbox workspace-write` blocks local IPC sockets, so a child cannot run checks that start `tsx`** — spec-kit's `npm --prefix runtime/cli run check` fails there with `listen EPERM`, also with `TMPDIR` pointed elsewhere (observed 2026-09-24 on codex-cli 0.156.1), and passes outside the sandbox. 247:- **`codex exec` defaults to `--sandbox read-only`** — file-modification tasks silently no-op (the agent plans changes but cannot write them). Pass `--sandbox workspace-write`; for headless no-prompt execution use top-level `-a never` before `exec` or `-c approval_policy=never`.
248:- **`--search` is a top-level flag, not an `exec` flag** — enable live web search as `codex --search exec …` (it precedes the subcommand). On codex ≥ 0.144 `codex exec --search` hard-fails with `unexpected argument '--search'` (older 0.125 builds accepted it), so treat any `exec … --search` example as stale. Without it, `codex exec` has no web access and answers from training data only — every dispatch needing live data (latest versions, repo facts, advisories) MUST use `codex --search exec …`.
251:- **`--sandbox workspace-write` blocks local IPC sockets, so a child cannot run checks that start `tsx`** — spec-kit's `npm --prefix runtime/cli run check` fails there with `listen EPERM`, also with `TMPDIR` pointed elsewhere (observed 2026-09-24 on codex-cli 0.156.1), and passes outside the sandbox. For unattended approval, put top-level `-a never` before `exec` or set `-c approval_policy=never`.
264:6. **Redirect codex stdin from `/dev/null` on EVERY non-interactive dispatch** — not only inside a `while read` loop, which is the condition this rule used to name and the reason it was skipped. Pattern: `codex exec "$PROMPT" > "$LOG" 2>&1 </dev/null &`. Without `</dev/null`, the backgrounded codex process inherits the loop's stdin (the file after `done < input.jsonl`) and silently consumes the remaining lines — the loop exits after 3-6 iterations with no error. See `references/integration-patterns.md#background-execution` → "Silent Stdin Consumption".

When an AI delegates via `codex exec`, the calling AI's own voice rules govern the response — do NOT read `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` and paste into delegation prompts.
